cases.quote: Note that JIS X 4051 specifies to not leave any spacing after the closing brackets (cl-02) or commas (cl-07) at the line end. Therefore, Table 4 also indicates that there is no opportunity for spacing reduction after closing brackets (cl-02) and commas (cl-07) at the line end. Likewise, because middle dots (cl-05) at the line end are supposed to have no spacing, Table 4 indicates there is no opportunity for spacing reduction for middle dots (cl-05) at the line end. On the other hand, while JIS X 4051 specifies to pad with a half em spacing after full stops (cl-06) at the line end, which is not allowed to reduce this spacing for line adjustment, Table 3 and 5 allow the removal of the default half em spacing after closing brackets (cl-02), full stops (cl-06) and commas (cl-07) at the line end for line adjustment. Table 3 further allows the removal of the default quarter em spacing padding before and after middle dots (cl-05) at the line end for line adjustment, while Table 5 does not.
cases.rationale: The legend's own worked example, read for the coordinate it names first: a closing bracket at the line end, carrying §B.2 note 2's preferred half em. The note states, in its own order, that Table 4 offers no opportunity to reduce it — JIS X 4051's own convention never pads it in the first place, so its table has nothing to drain — while Table 3 and Table 5 both remove it down to solid. §3.1.9 is why the drained reading is `discrete` rather than `range`: the closing-bracket line-end space is JLReq's own two-valued case, stated twice as "the possibilities are only half em spacing or solid," and this cell's own captured shape (two_valued, floor zero) is that fact read out of Table 3 and Table 5 alike. This is also the one coordinate at which the legend's own citation and the amount's own citation come apart: under Table 4 the space stays exactly where §B.2 note 2 put it, and the evaluator reports that note rather than this legend, because a boundary this project's own reduction table leaves untouched is reported by whatever fixed it, not by the legend that explains why nothing moved — the second permitted entry below states that reading rather than a `rule` field the runner does not compare.

permitted.source: JLReq §D.1, Table 3 (JLReq's own adopted method, §D preamble)
JLReq §D.1, Table 5 (a third method found in other publications, §D preamble)

forbidden.why: §3.1.9 states twice that the closing-bracket line-end space is two-valued — "the possibilities are only half em spacing or solid" — and this legend restates the identical amount as the same all-or-nothing drain under Table 3 and Table 5 alike. A continuously-shrinking reading is the value a naively continuous justifier emits and neither table's own answer to this boundary.
